input: Build a morning routine that sticks for real

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Wake-up time and available morning window determine what is even feasible to fit in — a 20-minute window needs a completely different plan than a 90-minute one.
Knowing which life areas the user wants the routine to serve (fitness, focus, calm, nutrition, etc.) defines what activities to include and exclude.
Whether the user lives alone, with a partner, or with kids changes constraints like noise, shared schedules, and interruptions that directly shape the plan.
Understanding why past routines have failed reveals the real blockers — whether it is inconsistent sleep, motivation, time, or something else — so the new plan avoids the same traps.
Some people thrive on rigid sequences; others need flexibility. The structure style determines how the routine is designed and how it is reinforced.
Knowing what 'sticking' means to the user — hitting it 5/7 days, feeling energised, completing every step — sets a measurable target to build toward.
Whether the user wants a written plan, an app, a physical checklist, or a coach-style accountability system determines the format and immediate first step.

gold.taskTitle: Build a morning routine that actually sticks
gold.taskDescription: Design and implement a consistent morning routine the user can realistically maintain long-term.

questions.title: What time do you need to wake up and leave the house?
questions.description: Establish the hard start and end boundaries of the morning window to determine how much time is actually available for the routine.

questions.title: Which areas of life should this routine improve for you?
questions.description: Identify the core goals the routine should serve — such as fitness, mental clarity, nutrition, mindfulness, or productivity — to define what activities belong in it.

questions.title: Why have your past morning routines broken down?
questions.description: Pinpoint the specific failure modes from previous attempts so the new plan is designed to avoid those exact traps.

questions.title: Do you share your mornings with a partner, kids, or housemates?
questions.description: Understand the household context to account for shared schedules, interruptions, and noise restrictions that affect what is realistic.

questions.title: Do you prefer a fixed sequence or a flexible set of options?
questions.description: Determine whether the user thrives with a strict order each day or needs a menu-style routine they can adapt based on how they feel.

questions.title: What would 'this routine is finally sticking' look like to you?
questions.description: Define a concrete, personal success benchmark — whether that is hitting the routine a certain number of days per week, completing all steps, or noticing a specific feeling.

questions.title: How do you want to track or be held accountable to the routine?
questions.description: Identify the preferred format and accountability system — such as a paper checklist, a habit-tracking app, or scheduled check-ins — to set up the immediate next action.
